name: Ex Vivo Breast Tissue Histological Subtype Classification (Ezzat et al. 2026)
description: Label-free Raman spectra of ex vivo human breast tissue (80 frozen tissue samples -- 46 normal, 34 cancerous -- from consenting donors via the Imperial College Healthcare Tissue Bank) for histological subtype classification: normal vs. invasive ductal carcinoma (idc) vs. invasive lobular carcinoma (ilc) vs. ductal carcinoma in situ (dcis). 641 spectra (177 normal, 221 dcis, 114 idc, 129 ilc) on a confocal Raman microscope (DXR3xi, Thermo Fisher Scientific), 785 nm excitation, 500-2,998 cm^-1 at a 2 cm^-1 grid. Tumor samples were measured at 3-6 spatial points, normal tissue at a single point, with 2-3 spectra per point. group_ids are the 80 tissue sample ids (sample_id format SXXX_MX_RX: sample / measurement point / repeat): the paper reports the 80 samples derive from 71 individuals (9 donors contributed two samples), but the deposit carries no sample-to-individual mapping, so sample level is the finest available group. One sample id (S076_M4_R1) appears twice with distinct spectra (two measurements); both rows are kept as deposited. The authors' analysis used an 800-2,000 cm^-1 region of interest with z-score normalization (see embedded_preprocessing); the deposit spans the full acquired range.
